transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-15
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Javier Morales (CTO - Polaris Tech), Priya Singh (Head of Platform), Ava Park (Procurement)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check-in today — we wanted to walk through renewal timing and the expansion asks you flagged, specifically the extra capacity and adding APAC region.
[00:18] Javier Morales: Yeah thanks Maya, appreciate it. We are a bit up against Q3 planning, so timeline is important. main ask is, can we get predictable capacity in APAC and a cost model for 3x what we run today, plus burst ability.
[00:34] Maya Chen: Totally. Liam and I have baseline numbers from your current committed capacity. we'll run through options: (hosted) extra reserved on Redwood Dedicated, or keep hosted and use burst credits. both have tradeoffs for cost and latency.
[00:50] Liam O'Connor: Quick note — for APAC we typically recommend pinning a dedicated pool if you need consistent p95 latency under 200ms for your customer-facing flows. otherwise you get hit with cross-region tails.
[01:07] Priya Singh: Can you remind me what the quantization / model variants implications are? we run mostly instruction-tuned open models, and we want to preserve quality.
[01:20] Liam O'Connor: Right — we surface model variants that are quantized and verified. for many workloads the 4-bit quantized variant keeps quality within expected bounds but reduces GPU footprint. we can include a quick eval on your prompt set during the benchmark.
[01:36] Ava Park: From procurement side, we need contract length options. do you support a 12-month extension with committed units and a monthly true-up? and what about price breaks for multi-region?
[01:50] Maya Chen: Yes, we can do a 12-month amendment. pricing tiers for reserved capacity scale — i'll prepare an amended SOW with 3x reserved capacity and APAC add-on. we'll include options for monthly true-up and burst buckets.
[02:05] Javier Morales: Security is top of mind — VPC peering, KMS support for keys, SOC 2 and audit logs. we might need on-prem/private later.
[02:18] Liam O'Connor: We support VPC private deployments and KMS integrations (BYOK). we'll attach the SOC 2 report and a VPC diagram. note: if you go fully private on-prem it's a different pricing and lead time.
[02:32] Priya Singh: Lead time is a concern — how long to stand up APAC Dedicated?
[02:40] Liam O'Connor: Typical provisioning for dedicated pools in APAC is 2–4 weeks once contracts and infra access are sorted. if you need faster we can provision burst capacity on hosted while dedicated is built out.
[02:57] Maya Chen: i'd also recommend running a short APAC perf benchmark with your representative prompts to validate p95 / cost per token. we can run that next week.
[03:09] Javier Morales: Sounds good. One more — do you have any capacity isolation between customers? important for compliance.
[03:18] Liam O'Connor: Dedicated capacity provides tenant isolation, separate GPU pools, and audit logs. we can enable stricter RBAC and token-level tracing in the console.
[03:31] Ava Park: Also curious: competitors — we ran a bake-off with ManagedCloud AI and Cohere; pricing looked similar but their APAC footprint was limited. any notes?
[03:44] Maya Chen: We saw mentions of Anthropic and Cohere — the main differentiators will be predictable unit economics and the rollout/observability features. we'll include a short comparison doc.
[03:56] Priya Singh: Ok on the technical side, if we bump to 3x reserved — what's the recommended autoscaling policy? we want to avoid paying for unused capacity.
[04:09] Liam O'Connor: We typically set baseline reserved capacity at ~60–70% of peak and use burst for spikes. autoscale policies allow scheduled scale-up and scale-down; the console exposes per-route metrics so you can tune it.
[04:25] Javier Morales: For billing, is there metering per token and separate metering for reserved vs burst? we need lines in our internal chargeback.
[04:36] Maya Chen: yes — reserved has a monthly commit plus per-token usage overages, burst is metered separately. we'll include token-level breakdowns in the quote.
[04:47] Priya Singh: Can Redwood support data residency in APAC? our users' data must remain in-region for certain flows.
[04:57] Liam O'Connor: We can restrict model hosting and KV cache to APAC via routing policies and region pinning, plus a private deployment if required. will need to capture which data needs to stay in-region.
[05:12] Maya Chen: quick note — transcription glitch: earlier in the doc i think it wrote "Redwood Dedicate" which should be "Redwood Dedicated" — small typos in the auto notes.
[05:22] (laughter)
[05:25] Maya Chen: Alright, let's talk timeline and owners. We'll draft SOW and pricing, Liam will attach security docs, and Javier will share traffic numbers so we can size the pool accurately.
[05:37] Javier Morales: i can have the traffic export by EOD Tuesday.
[05:42] Ava Park: Procurement would like to see a standard amendment template.
[05:46] Maya Chen: i'll include a clean amendment template.
[05:49] Priya Singh: For the APAC benchmark, can you include both quantized and full-precision runs? want to validate latency and quality tradeoffs.
[05:59] Liam O'Connor: yes — we'll run both, and include a small eval report against your prompt set.
[06:06] Maya Chen: Good. Any other objections or open concerns?
[06:10] Javier Morales: Nothing major. cost and contract terms are the last approvals.
[06:15] Ava Park: Just to confirm renewal date — our current contract ends 2027-05-31, so we'll need signed amendment before then to lock pricing.
[06:24] Maya Chen: Understood — target to have an agreed amendment by 2027-04-30 to allow internal approvals.
[06:31] Priya Singh: and run the APAC benchmark week of 2027-04-25 — that gives us numbers to make the commit.
[06:40] Maya Chen: Perfect. recap of next steps: Maya to send amended SOW and pricing (3x reserved + APAC), Liam to send SOC2 and VPC diagram and run benchmarks, Javier to send traffic estimates, procurement reviews amendment.
[06:55] Javier Morales: Thanks everyone.
[06:58] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the benchmark.
[07:04] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional auto-transcription errors and shorthand. References: SOW template link (shared in chat), security pack (SOC2.pdf), benchmark sheet (link to spreadsheet).
